Polyendocrine recognises that multiple hormone systems are involved, including insulin, androgens, and reproductive hormones. Metabolic highlights insulin resistance, one of the core drivers of the condition and a major reason why women with PMOS have a higher risk of type 2 diabetes and cardiovascular concerns. Ovarian reflects symptoms such as irregular cycles, anovulation, and fertility challenges.

You do not need ovarian cysts to have PMOS. Many women with normal ultrasounds can experience significant hormonal and metabolic dysfunction.

Studies estimate that PMOS affects 4-19.6% of women, yet millions remain undiagnosed because the condition often differs in every individual.
